summary: B1 revised Explore review completed with changes-requested. B1-RE-001 and B1-RE-002 are substantively resolved: the catalog now follows the frozen core-model spec's ten formal Change Actions, and ResultRef is provider-neutral without a mandatory Run path. One blocking internal inconsistency remains: the Review focus still instructs reviewers to require eleven Change Actions, directly contradicting the revised catalog, acceptance criterion, and conclusion. The Explore must have one executable review criterion before Proposal.

blockingFindings.title: Review focus retains the superseded eleven-Action catalog
blockingFindings.location: openspec/changes/domain-and-state-schema/explore.md:415; compare Q5, acceptance criterion 4, and conclusion 5
blockingFindings.evidence: Q5, the source-conflict resolution, acceptance criterion 4, and conclusion 5 consistently specify ten Change Actions and exclude change-checkpoint. Review focus item 4 instead says the catalog is complete only with eleven Change Actions plus two Delivery Actions. It was not updated when B1-RE-001 was resolved.
blockingFindings.impact: The same Explore both defines a conforming ten-Action implementation and directs its formal reviewer to reject it for lacking an eleventh Action. This leaves no single executable acceptance/review criterion for the Proposal or later Apply review.
blockingFindings.requiredResolution: Update Review focus item 4 to require the frozen ten Change Actions plus the two Delivery Actions, and explicitly check that review, revise, and change-checkpoint are absent. Recheck the Explore for any remaining eleven-Action wording that presents it as the required catalog.

resolvedFindings.resolution: Q5, section 6.5, acceptance criterion 4, and the conclusion now select the frozen core-model spec's ten formal Actions and treat Change Checkpoint as a Git boundary rather than an Action.
Q9 defines ResultRef through provider-neutral stable identity and version-fingerprint capabilities, without mandatory runPath; concrete serialization and adapter mapping remain C1 work.
